groups.title: Astro Component Model
groups.question: You are building an Astro card component that reads data and receives a title prop. Explain where its code runs and how props work.

followUps.Component Script Fence: Where does code inside the --- fence run?
followUps.Props and Component Composition: How do you type an Astro component's props?

evidence.text: Code in the frontmatter fence runs on the server or at build time.
None of it is sent to the browser.
It can fetch data and use secrets safely.

notEnough: Only saying the fence holds scripts.

evidence.text: A Props interface in the frontmatter describes the props.
Props are read from Astro.props.
TypeScript then checks how the component is used.

groups.title: Zero-JS by Default
groups.question: A client asks why your Astro site loads so much faster than their old React site, and you need a reusable page wrapper. Explain Astro's output and slots.

followUps.HTML-first Output: Why does an Astro page ship no JavaScript by default?
followUps.Slots and Template Composition: How do slots let a wrapper component accept content?

evidence.text: Astro components compile to plain HTML.
No JavaScript is sent unless a component explicitly needs it.
This gives a very fast first paint.
A slot marks where a parent's content is inserted.
Named slots allow several insertion points.
This is how wrappers and layouts are composed.

groups.title: Astro Templating
groups.question: A teammate tries to use an onClick handler in an Astro template and styles from one component leak into another. Explain how Astro templates and styles work.

followUps.Astro Template Expressions: Why doesn't an onClick handler work in an Astro template?
followUps.Scoped CSS in Astro: How does Astro scope component styles?

evidence.text: Astro templates use JSX-like expressions.
They are rendered to HTML on the server, not in the browser.
Event handlers need a script tag or a framework island.

notEnough: Only saying Astro is not React.

evidence.text: Styles in a component are scoped to it automatically.
Astro adds a unique attribute to keep them from leaking.
Global styles must be opted into explicitly.

groups.title: TypeScript in Astro
groups.question: A developer wants to turn off strict mode because of null errors, and a component is imported with the wrong props. Explain TypeScript in Astro.

followUps.Type-safe Component Imports: How does Astro catch wrong props on imported components?

evidence.text: Strict mode turns on null checks and stricter rules.
Turning it off hides real bugs instead of fixing them.
The errors point to places where values can be missing.
Imports are type-checked against the component's Props.
Wrong or missing props are reported before the build.
Running astro check catches these in CI.
